blocks.text: Imagine a structure where each node branches into two, creating a hierarchy that can efficiently store and retrieve data. Welcome to the world of binary trees!

blocks.markdown: Binary trees are a fundamental data structure in computer science, characterized by each node having at most two children. They form the basis for more complex structures like binary search trees and heaps.

blocks.title: Binary Tree
blocks.text: A binary tree is a tree data structure in which each node has at most two children, referred to as the left child and the right child.

blocks.markdown: The height of a binary tree is a critical concept, defined as the number of edges on the longest path from the root to a leaf. This height influences the efficiency of operations on the tree.

blocks.caption: The height (h) of a complete binary tree with n nodes.

blocks.markdown: Traversal of a binary tree refers to the process of visiting each node in a specific order. There are several types of traversal: in-order, pre-order, post-order, and level-order.

blocks.title: Traversal Types
blocks.text: In-order: Left, Root, Right; Pre-order: Root, Left, Right; Post-order: Left, Right, Root; Level-order: Level by level from top to bottom.

blocks.title: In-order Traversal Example
blocks.prompt:
Perform an in-order traversal on the following binary tree:

```
    A
   / \
  B   C
 / \
D   E
```

steps.text: Start at the root (A) and move to the left child (B).
Move to the left child of B (D), which has no children, so visit D.
Return to B, visit B, then move to its right child (E), which has no children, so visit E.
Return to A, visit A, then move to its right child (C), which has no children, so visit C.

blocks.title: Pre-order Traversal Example
blocks.prompt:
Perform a pre-order traversal on the same binary tree:

```
    A
   / \
  B   C
 / \
D   E
```

steps.text: Start at the root (A), visit A.
Move to the left child (B), visit B.
Move to the left child of B (D), visit D.
Return to B and move to its right child (E), visit E.
Return to A and move to its right child (C), visit C.

rows: Level by level from top to bottom
blocks.caption: Comparison of Binary Tree Traversal Types

blocks.markdown: Implementing these traversals can be done recursively or iteratively using a stack or queue. Recursive implementations are often more intuitive, while iterative ones can be more efficient in terms of space.

blocks.title: Recursive vs Iterative
blocks.text: Recursive implementations can lead to stack overflow for very deep trees, while iterative implementations using explicit stacks or queues can handle larger trees without this risk.

points: Binary trees have a hierarchical structure with each node having up to two children.
Traversals include in-order, pre-order, post-order, and level-order, each with a specific visiting order.
Recursive and iterative methods can be used for tree traversal, with trade-offs in space and simplicity.
